# Best portable power stations for camping

The best pick depends on how much you need to run, since the 250-500Wh class is the sweet spot for most trips, and bigger units suit fridges or multi-day stays.

**Weekend tent or car camping (phones, lights, camera, CPAP)**
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249, 288Wh, 8.3 lb) is PowerStationGearLab's top camping pick. Jackery's own US site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so check Amazon or other retailers for stock. [Review](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199, 288Wh) has a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Confirm you're buying the standard AC-outlet version, not the "DC" variant. [Review](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179, 268Wh, 600W AC) is the budget option. [Review](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

OutdoorGearLab's lab tests scored the small Jackery 300 and Anker C300 lower overall (52 and 50), mostly because of limited capacity. They're fine for phones and lights, but not for anything heavier. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)

**Mid-size (electric cooler, laptop, small appliances)**
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** was OutdoorGearLab's best value, on sale for under $530. It's compact but has a noisy fan. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** is TechRadar's pick for camping, with easy solar charging. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Bluetti AC180** has 1,152Wh, an 1,800W inverter and a 5-year warranty. It lists at $499 and weighs about 35 lb (16 kg). Dealectric's code AFF5OFF takes $24.95 off, which brings it to $474.05. [Buy at BLUETTI via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). This is an affiliate link, and the checkout price is the final word.

**Multi-day off-grid camping**
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** was OutdoorGearLab's top camping pick (score 81). It has 2,042Wh and weighs 39 lb, and it was recently under $900 on Amazon. It can't run a space heater or electric burner for long. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** was WIRED's camping pick. It's IP65-rated, has 1,536Wh, and was $1,079 on Amazon. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

**My suggestion:** For most campers, the Jackery Explorer 300 Plus or Anker C300 is enough. If you want a cooler or more than a weekend of power, step up to the Anker C1000 Gen 2 or Bluetti AC180.

The search results didn't include direct purchase links for most of these, so the links above go to the reviews. Search the model name on Amazon or the brand's store to buy. Prices come from the reviews and change often, especially with Black Friday sales coming up.

Roughly how many days will you camp, and what do you need to power? I can narrow it down from there.
